pitfalls: Timestral-209M's attention logits (up to 242,875) and RMSNorm sums of squares (up to 164,602,176) leave the float16 range (65,504): each RMSNorm input is pre-scaled by a power of two, the logits are computed at 1/16 with the row maximum subtracted before the scale is restored, the softmax input is clamped at -3*10^4 and the mask value is -3*10^4; in float32 these rewrites leave the results unchanged (card 'How the graphs were made').

Five float32 inputs, one signature `serving_default`: `patches` [2,256,64] (per patch 32 normalized values then 32 missing flags), `dec` [2,32,768] (`forecast_query.f32` for every decoder token), `bias` [1,1,288,288] (additive mask: 0 or -3*10^4), `cos` / `sin` [1,1,288,64] (rows cut from `rope_cos.f32` / `rope_sin.f32`) -> `output_0` [2,32,32,21], the normalized quantiles; the two rows are the series and its negation (card 'Inputs and output').

The graph is one step of the forecast: the host builds the inputs and finishes the forecast the way the official forecaster does (causal float64 scaling and asinh, the attention mask, the inverse map and the advancing refine frame, the caps at the context's range widened by 10^4 times the scale, symmetric averaging with the negation, clipping at 0 for non-negative series); the repository's `host_forecast.py` and `android/TimestralHost.kt` do it (card 'Inputs and output').

A file holds a context of up to 8,192 steps and a horizon of up to 1,024 steps (patches of 32): the host pads a shorter series in front with missing steps and keeps the requested steps; the smallest file that holds the series and the horizon takes the least time (card 'Files').

One series per forecast without covariates; a horizon of up to 1,024 steps (the Python class and the Kotlin host stop there; no result covers the official block-by-block decoding of longer horizons); of a series longer than 8,192 steps the last 8,192 are read (the official forecaster with max_context = 8192; its default is 32,768); the Python class refuses fewer than 16 values (card 'Limits').

The `-int8` files are the CPU files; the CPU runs the float16 files too, more slowly: on the Galaxy S26 CPU (4 threads) `timestral-209m-c8192-h1024-int8.tflite` takes 144.2 ms per forecast and `timestral-209m-c8192-h1024.tflite` 321.0 ms; most of their fully connected layers compute in int8, so their quantiles differ slightly from float32 (card 'Files', 'Speed on phones', 'Limits').
